authority.description: The :authority header in the gRPC request sent from Envoy to the extension service.
authority.rationale: Controls the :authority value sent to the authorization extension. Because this header influences which virtual host or service the request is associated with, a generic policy can restrict it to approved values to reduce unintended routing or trust-boundary issues.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Controls whether Terraform can destroy the resource. A generic policy can require PREVENT to reduce the risk of accidental or unauthorised deletion and protect the availability of the authorization control.

description.description: A human-readable description of the resource.
description.rationale: Provides human-readable metadata only and does not directly change authorization behaviour, network exposure, credential handling, or another platform-level security control.

fail_open.description:
Determines how the proxy behaves if the call to the extension fails or times out.
When set to TRUE, request or response processing continues without error. Any subsequent extensions in the extension chain are also executed. When set to FALSE or the default setting of FALSE is used, one of the following happens:
* If response headers have not been delivered to the downstream client, a generic 500 error is returned to the client. The error response can be tailored by configuring a custom error response in the load balancer.
* If response headers have been delivered, then the HTTP stream to the downstream client is reset.
fail_open.rationale: Directly determines whether requests continue when the authorization extension fails. A generic security policy can require fail_open to be false so authorization failures fail closed instead of bypassing the control.

forward_headers.description: List of the HTTP headers to forward to the extension (from the client). If omitted, all headers are sent. Each element is a string indicating the header name.
forward_headers.rationale: Controls which client headers are sent to the authorization extension. Because headers can contain credentials or other sensitive information, a generic policy can restrict forwarding to an approved set and avoid sending unnecessary sensitive headers.

labels.description:
Set of labels associated with the AuthzExtension resource.


**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.
labels.rationale: Labels are resource metadata used for organisation and management. They do not directly control authorization, exposure, encryption, or another generic security behaviour of this resource.

load_balancing_scheme.description:
Required when the service points to a backend service. All backend services and forwarding rules referenced by
this extension must share the same load balancing scheme. For more information, refer to
[Backend services overview](https://cloud.google.com/load-balancing/docs/backend-service). Possible values: ["INTERNAL_MANAGED", "EXTERNAL_MANAGED"]
load_balancing_scheme.rationale: Controls whether the extension is associated with an internal or external managed load-balancing scheme. This affects network exposure and trust boundaries, so a generic policy can restrict the scheme to approved values.

location.rationale: Determines the region where the resource is created. A generic policy can restrict deployment to approved regions for data residency, regulatory, and organisational security requirements.

metadata.description:
The metadata provided here is included as part of the metadata_context (of type google.protobuf.Struct) in the ProcessingRequest message sent to the extension server. The metadata is available under the namespace com.google.authz_extension.<resourceName>. The following variables are supported in the metadata Struct:

{forwarding_rule_id} - substituted with the forwarding rule's fully qualified resource name.
metadata.rationale: Metadata is transmitted to the authorization extension and can expose resource or request context. A generic policy can restrict sensitive or unauthorised metadata from being forwarded to the extension service.

name.description: Identifier. Name of the AuthzExtension resource.
name.rationale: This argument is only the resource identifier. The specific name does not define a generic platform-level security control.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: This argument identifies the GCP project containing the resource. Project identifiers are ownership references rather than generic platform-level security policy targets.

service.description:
The service that runs the extension.
The following values and formats are accepted:
* 'iap.googleapis.com' when the policyProfile is set to REQUEST_AUTHZ
* 'modelarmor.{{region}}.rep.googleapis.com' when the policyProfile is set to CONTENT_AUTHZ
* A fully qualified domain name that can be resolved by the dataplane
* Backend service resource URI of the form 'https://www.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{{project}}/regions/{{region}}/backendServices/{{name}}' or 'https://www.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{{project}}/global/backendServices/{{name}}}}'
service.rationale: This argument identifies or references the service that runs the extension. The correct service is deployment-specific, so it is treated as a resource or service reference rather than a generic policy target.

timeout.description: Specifies the timeout for each individual message on the stream. The timeout must be between 10-10000 milliseconds.
timeout.rationale: Controls how long the proxy waits for an authorization response. Excessive or unsuitable timeout values can affect availability and authorization failure behaviour, so a generic policy can constrain the timeout to an approved range.

wire_format.description:
The format of communication supported by the callout extension. Applicable only when the policyProfile is REQUEST_AUTHZ.
This field is supported only for regional AuthzExtension resources. If not specified, the default value
EXT_PROC_GRPC is used. Global AuthzExtension resources use the EXT_PROC_GRPC wire format.

Supported values:
- WIRE_FORMAT_UNSPECIFIED:
    No wire format is explicitly specified. The backend automatically
    defaults this value to EXT_PROC_GRPC.
- EXT_PROC_GRPC:
    Uses Envoy's External Processing (ext_proc) gRPC API over a single
    gRPC stream. The backend service must support HTTP/2 or H2C.
    All supported events for a client request are sent over the same
    gRPC stream. This is the default wire format.
- EXT_AUTHZ_GRPC:
    Uses Envoy's external authorization (ext_authz) gRPC API.
    The backend service must support HTTP/2 or H2C.
    This option is only supported for regional AuthzExtension resources. Possible values: ["WIRE_FORMAT_UNSPECIFIED", "EXT_PROC_GRPC", "EXT_AUTHZ_GRPC"]
wire_format.rationale: Selects the supported gRPC communication format for the extension. It primarily controls protocol compatibility and implementation behaviour rather than defining a generic platform-level security requirement.
